q1.boundary: The broker boundary around Catalog Management. ecommerce-catalog-service and ecommerce-image-service move from Redpanda (redpanda:29092) to Apache Kafka (kafka:29092); ecommerce-tenant-service, ecommerce-product-query-service and ecommerce-category-query-service stay on Redpanda. Every consumer x topic binding whose producer and consumer end up on different brokers crosses the boundary. Inside the boundary, catalog.product.events has two producers (catalog-service and image-service) and one inside consumer (image-service). Both producers and that consumer move together, so that binding does not cross.

q4.must_preserve: After the move, catalog-service must still receive TenantUpdated/TenantDeleted events that tenant-service (on Redpanda) publishes. That needs a redpanda->kafka flow for tenant.tenant.events under the same topic name, plus a consumer position on Kafka near its Redpanda position (offset 1). Without that position, auto-offset-reset=earliest replays the topic history. Tenant events drive per-tenant database provisioning and cleanup.

evidence.reference: docker exec redpanda rpk group describe ecommerce-catalog-service ecommerce-image-service ecommerce-category-query-service ecommerce-product-query-service

q4.must_preserve: After the move, image-service must keep receiving tenant lifecycle events from Redpanda via the same redpanda->kafka flow, from a translated position. Tenant deletion drives the image-service tenant cleaner, which wipes the tenant's S3 prefix, so missing or duplicated events have real effects.

Product-query must keep receiving product events from both producers that move: ProductUpdated/ProductDeleted from catalog-service and ProductImagePromoted from image-service. They arrive on Redpanda's existing catalog.product.events through a kafka->redpanda flow with the same topic name. The topic keeps its single partition and the product-id key, so per-product order is preserved. The group keeps its current Redpanda offsets, 120 at planning time. This binding feeds the storefront read model and its image URLs.

evidence.reference: docker exec redpanda rpk topic list

q4.must_preserve: Product-query must keep receiving AttributeUpdated events on Redpanda's catalog.attribute.events through the kafka->redpanda flow, so attribute data in product projections stays current. This binding is undocumented, so only the config, the source and the running group show it exists.

Category-query must keep receiving CategoryUpdated events on Redpanda's catalog.category.events through the kafka->redpanda flow, in order, from its current Redpanda offset (4 at planning time). This is the category read model the storefront reads.

Category-query must keep receiving AttributeUpdated events on Redpanda's catalog.attribute.events through the kafka->redpanda flow. This topic has two outside consumers, so the flow must carry it even though no document mentions it.

q5.statement: My evidence does not show that the move is lossless or exactly-once, and the plan makes no such claim. MirrorMaker 2 gives at-least-once copying between clusters. Offsets differ between source and target topics. Offset translation for tenant.tenant.events is approximate, so consumers may see duplicates or replays.

evidence.reference: MM2 source connectors produce asynchronously and translate offsets via sparse offset-syncs; no transactional guarantee across clusters.

q5.statement: I could not query the Kafka broker in this session; my kafka-topics.sh call was denied. I have not verified that Kafka is empty, how its listeners behave, or that MM2 can reach both brokers. The execution session must check all three first (plan item pre-1) and stop if a check fails.

evidence.note: Only the container config was read: shared-network alias kafka, advertised PLAINTEXT://kafka:29092, KAFKA_AUTO_CREATE_TOPICS_ENABLE=false.

q5.statement: Kafka has auto-create disabled. catalog.product.events, catalog.category.events, catalog.attribute.events and tenant.tenant.events.dlq must exist on Kafka before the moved services start. tenant.tenant.events.dlq is the DLQ that catalog-service and image-service write to on tenant-event failures. Not verified: whether the services create topics themselves or fail on a missing topic.

Not established: whether pods in namespace dev can resolve and reach kafka:29092. The pods reach redpanda:29092 today, and kafka sits on the same docker network, but I did not test it from a pod. Verify before the cutover.

Not established: whether the tenant-event handlers in catalog-service and image-service are idempotent. If the MM2 group-offset sync fails, the two groups on Kafka start from earliest and replay tenant.tenant.events (1 record now). After cutover, check that the Kafka groups ecommerce-catalog-service and ecommerce-image-service sit at the mirrored end offset and did not replay.

Not established: how the outbox behaves while catalog-service and image-service are scaled to zero. I assume unsent outbox rows in MongoDB are published to Kafka after restart and then mirrored to Redpanda. Verify with Redpanda end offsets: new end = previous end + records produced on Kafka.

evidence.reference: Outbox rows are tied to Mongo, not to a broker; the new broker address applies at the next flush.

q5.statement: Must verify after the move: image-service consumes the topic its own service publishes to, catalog.product.events, now on Kafka. Kafka's topic starts empty, so image-service's group on Kafka begins at offset 0 of new events only. It must have drained Redpanda catalog.product.events (lag 0) before it stopped, or it will miss image promotions.

evidence.reference: docker exec redpanda rpk group describe ecommerce-catalog-service ecommerce-image-service ecommerce-category-query-service ecommerce-product-query-service

q5.statement: Must verify after the move, through the operator's functional test and broker checks: an edit to a product, category or attribute, and an image promotion, all reach product-query and category-query on Redpanda; tenant events reach catalog-service and image-service on Kafka; groups ecommerce-product-query-service and ecommerce-category-query-service on Redpanda show lag 0 at the new end offsets.

q5.statement: MM2 needs IdentityReplicationPolicy to keep topic names unchanged. With that policy MM2 cannot detect cycles. Loop safety therefore rests on the two allow-lists being disjoint: tenant.tenant.events goes only redpanda->kafka, and catalog.* goes only kafka->redpanda. Re-check that after MM2 starts.

evidence.reference: IdentityReplicationPolicy does not prefix topics, so a topic allowed in both directions would loop.
